text.p: Salomon Brothers has increased its 1997 and 1998 earnings per share (EPS) estimates for Agan Chemical Manufacturers and maintained its buy recommendation, Salomon said in a report.
Salomon has raised its EPS forecast for 1997 to $1.96 against a previous forecast of $1.83 and for 1998 to $2.17 against a previous forecast of $2.07.
Salomon said Agan was expected to generate in 1997 additional revenues of $50 million to $70 million from recent acquisitions in Latin America and Southern Europe.
"For 1997 we forecast total sales of $353 million, an increase of 39.6 percent year on year...Agan is expected to increase sales from existing products by at least 10 percent year on year."
Agan and its parent company Makhteshim Chemical Works are the world's largest manufacturers of generic agrochemicals and marketers of crop-protection chemicals.
In September 1996 Agan and Makhteshim announced their intention to merge their operations into a newly formed holding company called Makhteshim-Agan Chemicals Holding (MACH).
"We continue to believe that the proposed restructuring will allow international investors better understanding of Agan-Makhteshim operations," said the report.
